scope: Read-only CPU construction of the production baseline renal anatomical column projector; byte counts of the exact GPU-bound typed arrays. No browser GPU allocation or peak VRAM measurement was performed.

steps: Build centerline segments from field.centerline, field.centerlineStride and field.arrays.centerlineEdges, retaining node IDs and radii.
Construct HybridContrastSystem({centerlineSegments}); compute per-edge flattened cell offsets.
Sum mesh.geometry.attributes[*].array.byteLength for raster buffers and inspect projection uniforms texture.image.data.byteLength for texture payloads. Keep CPU sampling attributes separate.

transferRisk.description: Any changed deformation vertices mark the entire BVH position texture dirty. Three r160 uploads its full 13,366,336-byte payload on next use, even for a small local change. At 15 acquisitions/s this is up to 200,495,040 payload bytes/s; this is bandwidth/driver pressure, not an identified growing allocation.

shaderReview.result: No reachable infinite loop or out-of-bounds array write identified for the built atlas.
bounds: Shared junction/path caches check capacity 16 before appending. Candidate mixtures check capacity 4 and fall back to an uncapped finite traversal.
Adaptive ray integration has 24 base intervals and maximum subdivision depth 4. Its four pending-right entries fit that bound even when comparisons involve NaN.
Junction and path BVH escape links are built in preorder and advance past the current node; finite node counts bound these traversals.
Lumen ray BVH uses a 64-entry shader stack; the MeshBVH builder default maxDepth is 40.
Outlet jet loop clamps count to 24; each path-membership list has a finite generated length.
hotspots: A nonuniform junction ray can evaluate many nested nearest-path and concentration queries, with up to 16 leaves per each of 24 base integration intervals.
Contrast target resolves up to 2048 x 2048 exact rays; overlap and broad active bounds can multiply shaded fragments. This can cause long GPU work despite bounded loops.

lifetimeReview.result: Projection dispose covers its BVH textures, index geometry, face/range geometry textures, junction textures, spatial textures and both integral histories. No growing allocation proven in this core path.
lifetimeReview.sharing: Raster position/coordinate/face attributes are borrowed from CPU sampling geometry, not copied into a second raster payload.

limitations: These are typed payload sizes, not total VRAM, driver-private storage, command-queue copies or peak resident memory.
Render targets other than the contrast target, bone and device geometry, C-arm context, debug buffers and DSA archives are excluded from the core total.
Source anatomy position/normal buffers are CPU-resident and may also become GPU-resident when used by debug rendering; they are not included in the contrast core GPU sum.
A large budget supports resource-pressure suspicion but does not establish out-of-memory as the cause of the reported context loss.
